59805.subject: Biology
59805.question_text: 1. (a) List three features which are essential for cross-pollination to take place (b) State three characteristics
59805.explanation: (a) The stigma and anthers mature at different times (i) Male and female parts of the flower are located on different plants (ii) Male and female flowers occur separately on the same plant (b) Petals are dull with no nectar of scent. Pollen grains are numerous, light, smooth and powdery so that they can be blown by the wind.

59815.question_text: Study specimens A,B, C and D carefully (a) ldentify specimens A and B without reason (b) Name the organism responsible for the damage observed on specimens A and B (c) List two ways by which each of specimens A and B can be properly stored (d) (i) ldentify specimens C and D without reason (i) List one animal or crop each that can be attacked by specimens C and D (ii) Explain how specimens C and D affect the crop or animal they infest (e) Name one way each by which a farmer can control specimens C and D (f) Make a labelled drawing 6-8 cm long of the dorsal view of specimen D.
59815.explanation: (a) Specimen A is a bean seed(s) Specimen B is tomato fruit (b) Th2 organisms responsible for the damage Observed on specimen A = weevil or beetle. Specimen B= fungus or mould or bacteria (c) ()) Specimen A (bean seed) can be properly stored through (i) Storage in air- tight polythene bags (ii) Storage in silos () Storage in cool dry place (iv) Storage in deep freezer or refrigerator (v) Seed dressing with chemicals or fumigants (vi) Seed processing (vii) Canning (i) Specimen B (tomato fruit) can be properly stored through () drying () canning or processing (iii) freezing (d) (i) Specimen C = Tick Specimen D = Termite (soldier) (i) Specimen C (tick) attacks goats, sheep, dog, man Specimen D (termite) attacks maize, palm tree, rubber, coconut and rice (ii) How Specimnens C and D affect the crop or animal they infest: Specimen C sucks blood from the animal and causes loss or blood (or anaemia) to the animal. It also transmits disease causing organisms to the animal. It causes itching and irritation to the organism. It predisposes animals to diseases Specimen D eats up the roots or stems or woody parts of plants. It then destroys or damages them. It also predisposes plants to diseases (e) Ways by which a farmer can control specimen C (tick) are byenimals graze. Ways by which a farmer can control specimen D (termite) are (i) by the use of insecticide (ii) through ploughing (digging) to remove the queen termite.

59816.question_text: (a) ldentify specimens E, F, G and H without reason (b) Name one excretory organ found in each o specimens E, F, G and H (c) (i) State the habitats of specimens E and H (i) Examine the limbs of specimen H. List two ways by which specimen H is adapted to the habitat (ii) Make a labelled drawing 8-10 cm long of specimen E
59816.explanation: (a) Specimen E = earthworm, Specimen F = cockroach Specimen G = twig of flowering plant. Specimen H=rat (b) The excretory organs found in specimens E to H are: Specimen E = nephridium or body surface. Specimen F= malphighian tubule. Specimen G= leaf or stem, Specimen H= lungs kidney and skin (c) The habitats of Specimen E and H are ()) Specimen E (earthworm) soil or damp soil or marshy area. Specimen H (rat) burrows or holes or bush or food stores or house or cupboard. (ii) Ways by which specimen H(rat) is adapted to its habitat are (i) Limbs end in claws for digging the burrow (ii) Forelimbs are short and muscular for absorbing shock on landing (iii) Hind limbs are long and muscular for running fast

59817.subject: Biology
59817.question_text: Specimens I and J are cross-sections of two plants whose cut ends were dipped in red ink or eosin (red dye) for at least 6 hours (a) Observe specimen I with the hand lens provided. Record your observation about the colouring of the tissues by the red ink or eosin.
59817.explanation:
(a) Observation after colouring the tissue by the red ink or eosin - The fing-like section is stained red. The remaining sections remain colourless (i.e others are not stained) (b) Observation after flooding with a drop of iodine for about one minute -A layer of ring-like tissue is stained blue-black or dark (c) () In (a) the tissue stained red conducts water and mineral salts (ü) In (b) the tissue stained active blue-black or black stores starch (d) Differences between the arrangements of tissues in specimen I and J

I dicot Stem

(i) Ring like vascular bundles (i) Presence of cambium (iii) Has wide cortex (v) Has distinct endodemis or starch sheath (v) Has distinct pith

J Monocot Stem

(i)Scattered vascular bundles (ii) Absence of cambium (iii) Has narrow or small cortex (iv) Has no endodermis or starch sheath (v)Has no distinct pith or has no pith
